lede: Friday was a green day for stocks on both sides of the Pacific. Jakarta and Wall Street climbed together, gold rose more than 2%, and yet crypto went the other way — Bitcoin slipped below $60,000 while the Fear & Greed index stayed pinned at Extreme Fear.

paras: The IHSG rose 1.84% to 5,338.46, a strong end to the week for Indonesian stocks. Bank Indonesia held its 2026 annual meeting, themed around synergy toward a stronger and more resilient Indonesia, while the Financial Services Authority (OJK) published its second-period 2026 list of sharia securities and released the results of Bank Indonesia's SukBI auction held the same day.
In a separate move, OJK revoked the business licence of PT Bank Perekonomian Rakyat Bontang, a small rural bank, in a reminder that the regulator is still cleaning up the sector's weakest lenders.

US stocks rallied the day after Thanksgiving, with the Nasdaq 100 leading the way, up 2.69% to 650.99. The S&P 500 gained 1.62% to 728.32 and the Dow added 1.26% to 507.60. Gold joined the rally, climbing 2.12% to $334.40.

Across the Atlantic, the European Central Bank published the decisions of its Governing Council and the results of its October consumer expectations survey, which looks at what euro area consumers expect for AI, jobs and prices.

Crypto did not join the rally. Bitcoin fell 1.08% to $59,923.10, slipping back below the $60,000 mark, and Ethereum dropped 1.62% to $1,662.48. The split left sentiment deeply fearful: the Fear & Greed index read 12, firmly in Extreme Fear, even as equity markets posted one of their best days of the week.
